title: Restoration phase of the round
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $start$ be one of its states, and let $w,s$ be Boolean words. There is a natural number $t\le 2|s|+|w|+5$ such that the split-search round body, started in the restoration phase from the cleanup-scan configuration at scan position $0$, reaches the restoration return state with candidate $s$ extended by one bit $1$ if $|s|\le |w|$, and otherwise with candidate $s$ unchanged. The run avoids the anchor state at every time from $0$ through $t$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
replaced:
For any input $w$ and candidate $s$, there is a time
$t \le 2\abs{s} + \abs{w} + 5$ such that the round body, started from the
restoration-phase embedding of the cleanup scan, reaches the canonical
anchored-word configuration in the restoration phase's return state carrying
one split-search step applied to $s$; the whole trace avoids the anchor.
